title: Migrate repo to bun (workspaces, lockfile, scripts, CI)
description:
Replace npm as the primary package manager with bun.

Scope
- Add bun.lockb and migrate existing package-lock.json usage
- Update root/workspace scripts to run via bun (and bunx where needed)
- Update CI/workflows to install deps and run gates via bun

Acceptance
- Fresh clone can run: bun install
- Root scripts work: bun run lint, bun run format:check, bun run typecheck, bun run test (API)

Notes

title: Add root dev runners (bun run dev/dev:staging) to start Caddy + web + api + worker
description:
Implement the one-command developer experience from repo root.

Decisions
- Local Caddy runs in Docker Compose and serves HTTP only.
- dev:staging uses Cloudflare Tunnel targeting Caddy (Caddy is the only entrypoint).

Scope
- Define bun scripts: dev (local) and dev:staging
- dev starts: Caddy (compose), web, api, worker (and optionally infra)
- dev:staging starts: dev + cloudflared tunnel (targeting Caddy only)
- Decide orchestration approach (plain bun scripts + concurrently vs Turbo)

Acceptance
- From repo root, bun run dev brings up all services with stable hostnames
- From repo root, bun run dev:staging exposes the same entrypoint publicly via tunnel
- Processes restart on change (web/api/worker) and exit cleanly
close_reason: Added bun dev/dev:staging runners; worker auto-restart; docs updated

Non-goals:

Notes:
- Current repo has per-folder env usage and a web-dev-server gateway; these will be replaced by Caddy + shared config.

- Replace api/src/env.ts + dotenv usage with packages/config
- Replace direct process.env reads across api/src (and drizzle.config.ts) with typed env

close_reason: Migrated API to typed shared env (no process.env reads); standardized origins; updated defaults/docs; tests pass

title: Refactor Web to use Caddy front door + PUBLIC_ env policy
description:
Align web/ (Astro) with the new Caddy-based routing and root-only env rules.

Approach (Astro official)
- Use Astro env schema (`env.schema` in astro.config.mjs) to declare client vs server vars and public vs secret.
- Use `astro:env/client` and `astro:env/server` imports in code, instead of ad-hoc `import.meta.env` reads.
- Env values still come from repo root (process env injected by the root runner / packages/config); do not add web/.env.*.

Scope
- Define env.schema for the variables web actually needs (e.g. API origin, Convex public URL)
- Replace `import.meta.env.*` access patterns in web code with astro:env imports
- Ensure browser code only uses PUBLIC_ (public) values; secrets remain server-only
- Make API calls use stable origin (API_ORIGIN) or relative paths behind Caddy

Acceptance
- Web runs behind Caddy (web.localhost) and calls api.localhost without CORS friction
- No secrets are exposed to the browser bundle
- No per-app env files are needed for normal dev
close_reason: Use Astro env.schema + astro:env for server API base; remove import.meta.env usage in web; default client calls to same-origin; docs/compose cleaned

title: Enforce env guardrails (ban direct process.env usage outside packages/config)

Add lightweight enforcement so the repo stays maintainable after the refactor.

Acceptance

- The rule has a documented escape hatch for tests/migrations when needed

close_reason: Reduced root scripts to dev/infra/apps + docker/staging + quality gates + convex; documented running api/worker directly via --cwd

title: Introduce shared typed env package (packages/config) with root-only layering
description:
Create packages/config as the single entrypoint for env loading + validation.

Scope
- Add Zod schema for required env vars (local/staging/production)
- Implement deterministic root env layering (.env.defaults + one of .env.local/.env.staging/.env.production selected by APP_ENV)
- Provide a helper to spawn child processes with the validated env (dev runner uses this so web/api/worker inherit root env without per-app .env files)
- Export typed env for Node-side consumers (api/worker/tools)

Astro integration note
- Astro will use its own `env.schema` + `astro:env/*` imports for client/server safety, but values come from this root env system (process env), not from web/.env.* files.

Acceptance
- Services crash fast with clear errors when env is missing/invalid
- No service reads process.env directly outside the env loader
- Root env files become the single source of truth
close_reason: Implemented packages/config env loader + schema + validated env spawn helper
